setlist_extra.title: That's It For The Other One

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hey Jude** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The Hey Jude encore is described as solid; Hey Jude sounds rough and out of tune, with Pigpen's vocal off key, as an encore [2][7][16]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer names The Other One, Dark Star and Doin' That Rag as standout performances; The show opens with a rocking Other One [10][18]
- **Saint Stephen** (2 reviews): Saint Stephen runs straight through The Eleven into Lovelight, with the band barely pausing between songs; The transition from Saint Stephen into The Eleven is singled out as especially good [7][10]
- **New Potato Caboose** (1 review): Around 5:25 into New Potato Caboose, Phil moves into a familiar-sounding classical jam [13]
- **Cosmic Charlie** (1 review): Cosmic Charlie leaps out of the speakers [18]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): During Dark Star, the attendee felt the room lift and spin into space like a rocket [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-03-01.sbd.16track.kaplan.4030.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 15 songs; 126 min; rated 5/5 by 29 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard recording's sound quality excellent; During the opening Other One, the room can be heard creaking on the tape [9][11]
- **gd1969-03-01.sbd.lesh-serafin.13584.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 120 min [2]
- **gd1969-03-01.sbd.nayfield.60.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 122 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: A reel flip in Lovelight leaves about ten seconds missing at the beginning [3]
- **gd1969-03-01.sbd.ashley-bertha.9391.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 125 min; rated 1.67/5 by 3 [4]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Bill Graham [1]
- Attendee recalls the Fillmore West ceiling being gold lamé [15]
- Pentangle and Sir Douglas Quintet are listed as other acts on the bill [2]
- Jerry plays acoustic guitar during Dupree's, Mountains of the Moon and the jam after [3]
- Reviewer considers this the best Other One of any show [14]
- Brent later played Hey Jude once in Canada on 3.22.90 [16]
- Hey Jude was probably first performed on 2/11/69, which appears on the multitrack release [17]
- Reviewer finds nearly every song top-shelf; rates 5/2/70 similarly, and prefers its Other One slightly [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-03-01.sbd.16track.kaplan.4030.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard from the 16-track master reel, to DAT, then CD and shn, via Aoxoa, Rango Keshavan and Seth Kaplan; Disc two is tracked for 80 minutes; info file notes patches for banter and tuning [1]
- **gd1969-03-01.sbd.lesh-serafin.13584.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SBD > DUAL 16-TRACK RTR @ 15 I.P.S. > 2-TRACK LESH VAULT MIXDOWN D > MCS D > SSSB [2]. Also: Soundboard played on dual reel-to-reel decks at 15 ips; Phil Lesh made a digital mixdown in 1998 [2]
- **gd1969-03-01.sbd.nayfield.60.shnf**: transferred by DAT>WAV by Rod Nayfield; source: Source: SBD 2-track reel > DAT > ZA2 > WAVs [3]. Also: Healy mixed the second set down from multitrack in the early vault release project [3]
- **gd1969-03-01.sbd.ashley-bertha.9391.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SBD>>MTMR>>DAT>>CDA>>DAW(Bertha>>CDA [4]

## Art and photos

- Photo by Caine Schneider (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - Fillmore West 1969: The Complete Recordings](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26756077694/) [20]
- Photo by Caine Schneider (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 3/1/69 Fillmore West, San Francisco, CA](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27265884962/) [21]
